page.layout: One column of italic verse, centred on the page; catchword at lower right below the last line.

p.i: Vera loquar, vanos fata indignantia fastus, Audacesque animos aliena in Regna ruentes Crediderim has nobis è coelo immittere pestes, Per solem hunc qui cuncta videt, per sydera iuro, Tempore quo prima sparguntur coerula luce Saepe mihi in somnis materna apparet imago Scissa genas, canosque manu laniata capillos, Nate age, carpe fugam, teque hinc, ait, eripe proceps, Rumpe moras, age, carpe fugam, nam funera classem Dira manent, rabiesque omnes absumet edendi Sic effata, sinum lacrimis, mare quaestibus implet. Scilicet haec olim dederat promissa Columbus? Scilicet has Vrbes, haec aurea Regna canebat? Et speramus adhuc, & inania vota fovemus? Cui Ligurum non nota fides, foecundaque fraudis Pectora! sed longo fac nos superesse labori, Et tandem optatos Indorum attingere portus, Indomitasque vltro sese submittere gentes, Ipse suo reget arbitrio Ligur omnia solus, Solus erit victor, Italisque imbellibus Vrbes Diuidet, & nostro quaesitas sanguine praedas, Illi aurum montes, subiectaque flumina mittent Nos humiles animae quas gloria nulla sequetur Horrendos rerum in casus, mortemque volentes Irruimus, nostri fructum feret ille laboris, Elatusque animo victis dominabitur Indis, Quin potius dum fata sinunt, nec dum horrida ponti

page.notes: The verse is printed as one unbroken block without stanza breaks, so it is one paragraph. The initial Q of "Quin" and the decorative C of "Columbus" are printed ornaments. The "&" signs are printed as the Latin ampersand-style sign. The bracket-like mark before "Saevit" is a printed mark and is not transcribed.
